generated_for: Sparrow Surfboards official named standup catalog

brands.name: Sparrow Surfboards
brands.short_description: North Shore Hawaii custom shortboards, fishes, guns, and logs from Sparrow.

models.name: 70s Single Fin
models.description: Built after working with North Shore legends, this is Sparrow’s smaller take on a classic Beak Nose Pintail with a 70s-style design that’s a bit more refined. Wave Size: Head High to Double Overhead

models.name: Baby Rhino 2.0
models.description: This is our Pre Mid Length board and this 2.0 version is more intended for deeper water waves. We’ve set loose a lot of different Rhino’s over the years and some have transformed into more of what might be considered a step-before or a step-down from more common “mid lengths”. Wave Size: Shoulder to Double Overhead for the fuller version; Overhead to Double Overhead for the thinner rail All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered

models.name: BonzA RiP slot
models.description: Our Version 2 of the BonzA model. A deep vee double spine that cuts out just behind the center fin. This, coupled with the slot rolling outwards on this model, gives the board more release to perform tighter maneuvers. The projection out of the bottom and out of cutbacks feels like an accelerator on these designs, which is great for those longer arching turns. For this design, Sparrow wanted to make those arching turns to be a little tighter when desired. So these changes and the round pin tail help the rider get a little more snappy. For fin setup, the go-to is the same recommendations as the diamond tail model, the bonzer-esque style quads with a center box fin . We like these leaf shaped fins after experimenting with a few different options. And, for the center, we like this Island Fin Design Wingnut fin at about 5.5-6.5 inches tall. A standard quad option can be considered if you want to customize the order. Wave Size: Shoulder to Head High plus This model defaults to standard glass with glass-on quad fins, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: BonzA Slot Diamond
models.description: Reintroducing this unique-feeling, bonzer-inspired board. It’s not a fish, though it kinda paddles like one, and it’s definitely not a typical shortboard. If you’ve tried other bonzers then you know there’s something to them, but sometimes they’re just missing a little something. That’s what Sparrow was going for here. This board has a wider diamond tail that would otherwise feel super loose and skatey, but the bottom contour is where the magic happens. A deep vee double concave in the last third of the board with a prominent spine running through the tail pulls the board back down to the water, giving control back to what otherwise would be loose and wild. There’s something so fun to these bottom contours and the feeling that they give. Wave Size: Waist to Head High (plus a lil) This model defaults to standard glass with glass-on quad fins, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: Classic Gun
models.description: Our Classic Gun is a favorite for some of Sparrow’s earlier Gun clientele. There are no bells and whistles, none of that Step Deck New Aged Crap! Just a modern gun that has smooth curves, an easy deck foil, nice tapered rails, a slight vee bottom rolling into a deeper vee, a well balanced rocker, and just a standard nose (no beak necessary). The guys that helped Sparrow refine this design are quite humble, underground chargers that frequent the outer reefs on the North Shore and love to escape the crowds while everyone else is trying to get their picture taken..…But please send us your pics! ;) Wave Size: Shoulder High to Double Overhead…maybe a lil more depending on Dimensions All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: Ghost Fish
models.description: This is Sparrow’s more “True Fish”. It’s designed primarily as a twin keel fin with the fins pulled further back on the tail. The fin setup, the wider deep swallow tail which straightens the tail outline, and the lower tail rocker, make this board rocket down the line when given the proper input. In terms of length, this design is best ordered at the lower limits of what you’re comfortable with, but go a bit wider and towards the upper limits of thickness that you’re comfortable with. For example, if your “go-to” performance shortboard is a 6’2 x 19 1/2 x 2 1/2, you might like a 5’6 x 20 1/2 x 2 3/4 Wave Size: Waist to Head and a Half

models.name: Mini Gun
models.description: Our Mini Gun is between our step-deck shortboard and a gun. Wave Size: All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: SpaceTime Fish
models.description: This is Sparrow’s newer Fish design. Pulled from years of design modifications, this board is inspired by an early 2000’s, pluggy nugget-type fish. It has a wide tail block but shorter swallow cut into it, which is accompanied by a fairly parallel outline. The tail rocker is on the lower side while the nose rocker has a little extra kick out the last 10 inches. The rocker through the middle forward (before the kick) is extended to help make this a paddle machine and also to extend the sweet spot forward a bit. The rear half of the board features our StepDeck and a very slight hump (Like a vee double on the deck side) to give it that pre-settled feeling under the back foot. It can handle close to double overhead under the right feet and won’t feel like it’s too loose or going to slide out. It can drive fast down the line, and it can pivot to the top and snap if you want to get after it. The recommended fin set up is 5 fin with keels up front and small 3 inch fins in the rear. It goes best as either a twin plus a trailer or twin plus quad trailers. It can be ridden really loose as a twin keel, but the Keel Thruster option or Keel Quad are what is most often desired. Those trailers give the board a touch more oomph while holding through turns or rifling down the line. This is generally ordered really short. If your “go to” performance shortboard is a 6’2 x 19 1/2 x 2 1/2, you might like a 5’7 x 20 1/4 x 2 3/4. Carbon Fiber or Standard Epoxy is a great choice for this model. Wave Size: Shoulder to (just under) Double Overhead

models.name: Sun Fun Gun
models.description: More Gun than Fun. Sparrow’s Sun Fun Gun was specifically designed with team rider Trevor Carlson. It was directed towards more solid and powerful waves (ie: Sunset Beach). Trevor and Sparrow were going for something that could work well on days where you didn’t quite want to take a mid-sized gun out, and something that would work on the bigger days where you could sit inside a little and take the ledgy ones. It has since morphed into many different variations. Some with a Step Deck, some with wider tails to make them a little more friendly in smaller waves too. But this Sun Fun Gun is built for juicy stuff and has lots of hold with its narrower tail. Entry rocker is low, to give the ultimate glide into the wave. The point of the design was all about getting in early with that lower nose rocker. It’s the kind of board where you want to glide in a little behind the peak and take a nice high line as you set up the rest of the ride. Wave Size: (near) Double Overhead to Double Overhead Plus All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Alternate
models.description: The alternative shortboard between your chipped-out shortboard and a “groveler” small wave board. This is the modern performance board we’ve been continuously dialing in over the years. It has a little more nose width than a blade, and a nice, even rocker and rail line to maintain speed while allowing for more vertical turns in the pocket. Wave Size: Waist to Head High (plus a lil) All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Animal
models.description: All-around everything shortboard. It’s a beast that works in most conditions. The entry rocker is lower but not so low that you can’t fade straight to the bottom on a steeper drop. It took us years and a lot of trials to find that happy medium between nose rocker and optimal nose width. The back half of the board is very performance-oriented, with the tail ever so slightly wider than other shortboards. It’ll give you that little extra pushing back feeling you get from a wider tail, with the hopes of giving you that drive and projection you’re going for. We have a few riders who consider this their main board and they’ve been consistently ordering and building their quivers around this “Animal” design for years. Wave Size: Shoulder High to (close to) Double Overhead All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The NaySayer (StepDeck Gun)
models.description: This design is the result of 16 years of gun-building with team rider Trevor Carlson (Sparrow’s human guinea pig) and years of experience and knowledge that Sparrow gained from legendary North Shore board builders. The Step Deck Gun is a space-aged rocket ship. We highly recommend this in our Carbon Epoxy Construction. All the elements have come together to make this one of the most trusted high performance guns that is built. We don’t have the super star surfers out there pushing our brand, just solid watermen and water women out there that know what we are about. These guns have had so much time and heart put into them both in and out of the water, and we really want to keep pushing them to the limits. So whether you want to push your personal limits or just have the trust that this big wave machine will make the drop and do the job, consider a Sparrow Gun and thank Trevor for making this board a reality. Wave Size: All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Noserider Swoop
models.description: Aptly named after the arm motions you’ll make while riding this board. It’s a log, but not a brick of a log. It has that classic 50/50 rail feel but is still agile. Sparrow wanted to take a classic longboard outline and slightly modify the bottom contours and rocker to make a nose rider with a little more character. This board generates a little more speed than some of the traditional, full-belly logs out there and it has that swoop-around feeling when the rider steps back on the tail. This noserider is also not a plank. It actually has nose rocker to it! We found the perfect amount of rocker for those that want to get out to the nose and hang out there for awhile, but also you don’t have to worry as much about sticking the nose in steeper, more vertical sections. Sparrow was actually surprised at how much nose rocker this board could handle while still performing as desired. The outline features wider hips in the back third of the board, which helps send the rider naturally towards the nose (it basically makes you feel like you’re able to walk forward more comfortably. The nose is on the narrower side (You don’t actually need a wider nose to nose ride, common misconception). This is definitely a fun, fun, fun board to have in your quiver. Order them thick!! The rails are tapered and not blocky. Some longboards aren’t as thick through the middle and carry more foam out to blocky rails. This design isn’t like that. The deck has a nice rolled foil to it, allowing the centerline to hold more foam and thus making the rails feel more connected in the face of the wave. And this allows the board to actually be pushed in bigger surf if desired. Wave Size: (Ankle Slappers to Head and a Half +?) This model defaults to standard glass, single fin unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Performance Butter Knife
models.description: So you are a longboarder and rip, or you want a longboard designed to rip. This is your guy… or you girl…or your…This Longboard can work in junky waves, but it excels in the good stuff. We took our Performance Longboard and made it better with the help of team riders like Jack Ho, and we’ve since put it to the test with excellent surfers like himself and others. This board goes well with standard glass, but for ultimate durability we recommend this with our Carbon Epoxy glasswork. Rails are medium thin. Wave Size: Shoulder to Double Overhead

models.name: The Performance Shortboard
models.description: After years of refinement on the North Shore, this board is meant for the best days and the best conditions. Pure performance for those who want a modern design, pulled from nearly 20 years of working on the North Shore with Hawaii’s best surfers and shapers. This board came from listening to the consistent design ideas that enable a shortboard to perform at its best in some of the world’s top surfing conditions. Wave Size: Shoulder to Double Overhead

models.name: The Pleasure
models.description: This is the one for an all-around mid length, mid-range, middle of the road board, whatever you want to call it! A good ole, mid-sized board that works well in little-to-no feet and then all the way up to as far as you want to push it (double overhead no problem). The rocker is balanced and natural. It’s designed with just enough rocker to get you out of situations where you might pearl, and it’s not so high that you’re pushing water when you paddling. It can be surfed both friendly and mellow or with a little more oomph! 7’6 was the master design, but Sparrow has taken this design from 6’6- 8’0. All the sizes perform. Our main sizing is listed below, but we’re very happy to customize this one for you. Typically ordered as a 2 plus 1 fin setup. Wave Size: Ankle biters to double overhead This model defaults to standard glass, Future fins, 2 plus 1 fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Rascal
models.description: This is our performance fish - a fish that’s not so much a fish. It’s somewhat like a grovel-type board, but it likes good waves. It’s snappy in the pocket and prefers to stay in the hook of the wave. Look more towards our other fish varieties if you’d rather have something that handles flatter soft sections or if you’re looking to draw out longer arching turns. This model likes to go top to bottom and to be pushed around. Wave Size: Shoulder to Head and a Half High All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The Step Aside: Step Deck Shortboard
models.description: This board is designed to pack in some extra foam but still has the on-rail drive feel of a thinner board, with the rail more locked into the wave. This idea was pulled from Sparrow’s original ideas for his bigger-wave boards and guns. When applied to our shorter boards and fish mods, the Step Deck is felt most on waves that tend to have a bit more of vertical wall, allowing the thinner mid-rail between the feet to really set into the wave, whereas a boxed-out, fuller rail could resist the input from the surfer. On these shorter boards, the effect is much more subtle, and it’s really felt more as the boards get longer. It’s definitely a nice compromise for getting that extra paddle volume. Wave Size: All Sparrow boards on the site default to standard glass, Future fins, 5-fin setup, unless otherwise specified or custom ordered.

models.name: The StickBird (All-Around Longboard)
models.description: Built to be forgiving, to catch waves easy, and be easy and fun to surf in most conditions. The rails are medium rails, still not as full as many generic longboards, and like many of our bigger board designs, we don’t shy away from foam in the middle of the board, but we like to taper our rails so they aren’t blocky. Why not have volume in your longboard?! We want you to have as much extra paddle power as you can, without taking away from the ride.

models.name: Z-Spear
models.description: A newer model designed on the concept of down-the-line speed. Sparrow lowered the tail rocker and brought the hips out to give a more parallel outline through the mid section. The idea was to create as much immediate drive as possible to get through sections with a little extra boost. The bump wing breaks the tail free, allowing the board to pivot. This gives the design the best of both worlds, speed and maneuverability. The Z-Spear is often ordered as wing-pin and in epoxy, but other tails work with this design, such as a wing-swallow or diamond tail. Wave Size: Shoulder to double overhead
